$comment: Provenance: read from courier at a8f15ccef11bd6148c71fbe38327d9fbebbfe2e2, from `Courier.Events.complained/1` in lib/courier/events.ex. Field for field the same payload as `bounced/1`, which is why the two schemas differ only in title and description. The commit is fleet.yml's sourceCommit for courier.
title: courier.email.complained payload
description: The `data` payload of the `courier.email.complained` event: the recipient marked the message as spam. This is stronger evidence than a bounce and it arrives later — a complaint is a person, not a server. courier's manifest declares this type before it has a provider webhook to receive one, so the payload is the four fields `courier.email.delivered` carries and no provider diagnostic. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

message_id.description: The notification that was complained about. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`, and read back out of the `Message-ID` header the send set.

user_id.description: The user who complained. A uuid from identity, not a anywaye-prefixed id: see D7.

notification_type.description: Which of courier's messages this was. courier registers its types at boot (config or COURIER_NOTIFIERS_DIR), so the set is not frozen here.

email.description: The address that complained. Suppressed immediately, with no retry and no bounce to wait for.
